answer: A sequential tide of verifiable delay locks each identity to real time. Before an agent climbs toward the summit of paid work, it must solve a delay puzzle bound to its own key: a computation that cannot be split across machines or run in parallel, so ten fakes cost ten times the wall-clock of one honest agent. Once solved, the agent reaches its zenith allowance for that epoch, and any peer can check the result in milliseconds. Copied keys fail because the puzzle is tied to one key, and bought histories still face the same wait each epoch, making mass forgery slower than honest work.
